extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: The largest open dataset for language model pre-training. The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones rarely present in pre-training datasets; in addition, it includes a large portion of code data.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian, and others
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is an aggregation of various collections: Open Government (financial, legal, administrative data), Open Culture (cultural heritage datasets, monographs, periodicals), Open Science (scientific papers, theses), Open Code (code data), Open Web (Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube transcripts, StackExchange), and Open Semantic (Wikidata). Data was collected using APIs, standard retrieval methods, and large dumps from sources like Collections As Data (CAD), Internet Archive, Delpher, OpenAlex, The Stack, and Wikimedia.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. The amount of collected data (2 trillion tokens) is suitable for pre-training of models of limited size; larger models will require significantly larger amounts of data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Collections As Data (CAD) dumps, Internet Archive, Delpher, OpenAlex, The Stack v1 and v2, Wikimedia Enterprise HTML dumps, YouTube videos, StackExchange forums, Wikidata RDF triples, SEC EDGAR, WTO Documents Online, AMF, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc, French open data, USPTO, UN Digital Library, OECD.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: PII is replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Documents containing harmful language are either removed or synthetically rewritten without the harmful language. OCR errors are corrected using OCRonos, which can act as a synthetic rewriting tool on highly deteriorated content.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PII replacement with fictitious values. Synthetic rewriting of harmful language. Translation of Wikidata items and properties into natural language sequences.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation using Segmentext. OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerror. OCR correction using OCRonos. PII removal using Microsoft Presidio with custom regex patterns. Toxicity detection and filtering using Celadon. Filtering by license, language, and file format. Removal of files with 75% or more digits. Replacement of sequences of [\r]+\n with \n.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Toxicity annotation using Celadon, a DeBERTa-v3-small model trained on 2M annotated samples, identifying toxic content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Presidio, Celadon, OCRoscope, OCRerror, OCRonos, Segmentext, cld2
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses are identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to support the pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs, making it legal to release the source even without the provision of fair use. Addresses negative externalities affecting competing markets, the digital commons, and society at large caused by copyrighted training data. Mitigates the reproduction and circulation of harmful language from historical texts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical texts in Open Culture may not meet modern ethical standards regarding the discussion of certain ethnic groups, women, and themes such as violence. Web data sources can contain sexual content, hate speech, and racial and gender biases. The dataset suffers from the 'open data paradox' where major sources of open content are paradoxically little visible online.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Far from covering the entire range of available open resources (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. Data volume (2 trillion tokens) is suitable only for limited size models; larger models need more data. Does not contain data for instruction-tuning or specialized tasks. Curation methods (OCR, PII, toxicity) do not have 100% accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs. Development of vision-language models (VLMs) for advanced document segmentation and processing. Training models with legal knowledge. Document processing in official administrative applications. Training multilingual language models with diverse and creative writing styles. Development of historical language models. Coding applications. Improving model performance on natural language reasoning, world knowledge tasks, mathematics, and structured output tasks.
